ProbabilityTheory.IsUniform.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space and $S$ a type. For a set $H\subseteq S$, a function $X:\Omega\to S$ and a measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ (by default the canonical measure of $\Omega$), $\mathrm{IsUniform}(H,X,\mu)$ is the proposition (a structure with a single constructor) that both of the following hold: (1) for all $x,y\in H$, $\mu(X^{-1}(\{x\}))=\mu(X^{-1}(\{y\}))$ (as values in $[0,\infty]$); and (2) $\mu(X^{-1}(S\setminus H))=0$. No assumptions are made on $H$ (it need not be finite or nonempty), on $X$ (it need not be measurable) or on $\mu$ (it need not be a probability measure). According to its docstring, it is intended to express that the law of $X$ is the uniform probability measure on a finite set $H$.
